gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.de: Green: deployed; dim: owned but benched or not owned
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.un: 2 Undead: on death, deal magic damage equal to 10% maximum health to enemies within 2 blocks.
4 Undead: Undead gain 25% attack damage, and basic attacks heal for 2.5% maximum health.
6 Undead: revive once at 35% health with an empty skill bar.
8 Undead: skill charge gain +40%, and revival health increases to 50%.

10 Undead: immediately gain one Ender Dragon from the shared pool. Each later stage that still has 10 Undead grants another until all 9 shared copies are taken. Ender Dragons never appear in the shop and otherwise follow normal unit rules.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.be: 6 Beast: basic attacks deal an extra 5% of the target's current health as physical damage, once per target every 2 seconds and capped at 400.
8 Beast: all allies gain 25% attack damage; Beasts gain another 30% attack speed.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.ne: 2 Nether: basic attacks apply 2.5 seconds of burn and Grievous Wounds.
6 Nether: when hit, apply 4 seconds of burn and Grievous Wounds to the attacker; on death, explode within 1.75 blocks for 12% maximum health.
8 Nether: gain another 10% attack damage; basic attacks heal for 15% of damage dealt.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.oc: 2 Ocean: magic resistance +30, heal 4% maximum health every 5 seconds.
3 Ocean: start combat with a shield equal to 30% maximum health; take 20% less damage while shielded.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.en: 2 End: dodge +25%; the next basic attack after a dash or teleport deals an extra 60% attack damage.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.ar: 2 Arthropod: basic attacks apply Poison IV for 3 seconds.
3 Arthropod: deal 25% more damage to poisoned targets; skills also apply Slowness III for 4 seconds.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.co: 3 Construct: start combat with a 25% maximum-health shield; take 10% less damage while shielded; breaking it stuns enemies within 1.5 blocks for 1.5 seconds.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.vi: 4 Villager: when a Villager dies, the nearest ally gains 30% attack damage and 25% attack speed for 7 seconds.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.il: 2 Illager: deal 25% more damage to targets below 60% health.
4 Illager: skill hits apply 4 seconds of Grievous Wounds, armor break and 25% magic resistance reduction.

6 Herd: every 5 seconds grant the lowest-health ally a shield equal to 10% maximum health.
8 Herd: all allies gain 10% attack speed.
10 Herd: all allies gain 15% attack damage; Herd units start combat with a 15% maximum-health shield.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.gu: 3 Gunner: every fourth basic attack deals an extra 100% attack damage.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.su: 2 Summon: summons gain 40% health and 30% attack damage.
4 Summon: summoning or splitting grants all allies 20% attack speed and movement speed for 7 seconds; summons inherit another 30% of the summoner's magic power.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.gu: 4 Guardian: take 15% less damage; every 5 seconds grant the lowest-health ally a shield equal to 12% maximum health.
6 Guardian: all allies take 12% less damage; Guardians start combat with a 30% maximum-health shield.
gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.ar: 2 Arcane: magic power +40 and restore 1 extra skill charge every second.
4 Arcane: skill damage +25%, skill charge gain +20%, and restore 2 extra skill charge every second.
6 Arcane: total skill damage bonus increases to 55% and restore 3 extra skill charge every second.
9 Arcane: total skill damage bonus increases to 115% and restore 5 extra skill charge every second.

4 Bulwark: Bulwark units take 10% less damage.
6 Bulwark: breaking a Bulwark shield stuns enemies within 1.75 blocks for 2 seconds.
10 Bulwark: all allies take 8% less damage; Bulwark units start combat with a 25% maximum-health shield.

gui.monster_conquest.arena.game.trait.ca: 2 Caravan: losing a real match adds 1 stack. Only the current highest tier applies. Stack cap 6; cash-out is 2 gold per stack. At 3 stacks gain a Lesser Unit Duplicator, at 5 a random base component and at 6 a random special item.

3 Caravan: losing a real match adds 1 stack. Only the current highest tier applies. Stack cap 18; cash-out is 3 gold per stack plus 1. At 3 stacks gain 2 Lesser Unit Duplicators, at 5 2 random base components, at 7 2 random special items and at 8 2 Unit Duplicators.

4 Caravan: losing a real match adds 1 stack. Only the current highest tier applies. Stack cap 24; cash-out is 4 gold per stack. At 2 stacks gain 3 Lesser Unit Duplicators, at 4 3 random base components, at 6 3 random special items and at 8 a Unit Duplicator; each stack above 8 grants 1 more Unit Duplicator.

6 Caravan: losing a real match adds 1 stack. Only the current highest tier applies. Stack cap 999; cash-out is 5 gold per stack plus 3. At 2 stacks gain 4 Lesser Unit Duplicators, at 3 4 random base components, at 5 4 random special items and at 7 2 Unit Duplicators; each stack above 7 grants 1 more Unit Duplicator.

guide.monster_conquest.chapter.rts.body:
#Entering RTS
- Press {key.rts} to enter / leave the RTS command view; the selection is kept, so you can pick up where you left off.
#Selecting
- Left-click a soldier: units in a squad select the whole squad, lone units select only themselves; drag with the left button to box-select.
- Double-click selects every soldier of the same kind (e.g. all zombie soldiers); Ctrl+double-click selects the same troop type (melee / ranged / dual / thrower / gunner, gunners split by gun); Ctrl+click adds to the selection.
- Middle-click switches free / fixed camera.
#Orders (right-click)
- Right-click ground to move, an enemy to attack, a friendly unit to follow it.
#Hotkeys
- Cavalry form {key.cavalry}, infantry form {key.infantry}, formations {key.formation1} ~ {key.formation5}.
- The command wheel ({key.wheel}) offers finer orders.
#Display
- Selected soldiers are marked and the move target is shown on the ground (it fades after about 15 seconds).
guide.monster_conquest.chapter.logic.bod:
#Threat and hatred
- When a unit is attacked or ordered to attack, threat spreads to its army and same-faction reinforcements, so the whole army locks onto the target.
- Hatred does not expire just because a path is long: it only expires when the target is truly unreachable.
- Faction hostility comes from the config and the N-key faction screen; the Hatred Wand adds temporary hostility (Shift+Left-click clears in-game hatred).

#Patrol captains
- A patrol captain spawns with 3 soldiers; while it has fewer than 3, it adopts nearby orphan soldiers of the same faction, never exceeding 3 soldiers in total.
- Adoption drop-off points are safety-checked too (never on roofs, in pits or on hazardous blocks).

#Converting mobs into soldiers
- Commanders and patrol captains can convert the vanilla creatures listed in the config into their own soldiers; each faction has its own toggle under factionConversion in factions-common.toml (undead / illager are on by default, the rest are off).
- A rule may list several target types separated by | and picks one at random, e.g. the illager faction turns pillagers into one of the four gunners.
- Adopting same-faction orphan soldiers is always enabled and is not affected by these toggles.

#Pathfinding
- When you order a unit to a point (single unit move, commander march, squad move), if vanilla pathfinding cannot get there (maze / walls / too long a detour) it automatically switches to a block-level A* route and walks the waypoints out; orders for a whole squad are planned in small batches instead of all on the same tick.
- While marching only the commander plans a route; soldiers queue along the trail it walked and only chase the commander directly when more than 16 blocks behind.
- Units climb ladders / scaffolding / vines: when their goal is above and a climbable block that leads up is right next to them, they climb it; mounted units dismount first and will not remount while climbing.
- Walls and mazes are bypassed with a block-level A* detour: it goes around walls and through wooden doors / fence gates, but never climbs fences or 2+ block ledges.
- A unit that fell behind its follow range paths back first (walking home whenever a route exists) and only teleports when it is truly stuck and no route exists at all.
- Stuck detection combines the absolute distance (am I getting closer?) and the path distance (does a route still exist?):
  - no route at all (e.g. trapped in a pit): after about 10 seconds it escapes upward to an open spot (never next to the enemy);
  - a route exists (even a long detour): treated as a detour, no teleport, only re-planning;
  - truly not moving (blocked by terrain): side steps / doors / dismounting first, then a recovery teleport.
- In combat, an enemy that is unreachable, or clearly higher up (wall top / tower, more than 2 blocks above), is never teleported to: the unit blacklists that target for about 30 seconds and fights what it can reach instead.

#Melee range
- Melee units can only hit enemies on roughly their own level (about 2.4-3 blocks horizontally, at most 1.5 blocks of height difference): standing on a wall or tower keeps you out of melee reach.
- Archers and gunners can still shoot upward; a lance charge allows up to 2 blocks of height difference.

#Mounting
- Soldiers mount on open terrain and dismount in narrow or low passages; they dismount early when the way ahead is too tight for a horse.
- On ladders / scaffolding / vines they never auto-mount or force-mount until they step off the climbable block.

#Peaceful
- On Peaceful difficulty units are not removed, but they gain no hostility or hatred and never attack each other; in-game hatred is cleared.
- To match vanilla monsters, set peacefulRemovesUnits = true in general-common.toml: units are then removed on Peaceful difficulty.
- Summon commanders, patrol captains and soldiers of any faction with spawn eggs (soldier eggs cycle factions and cavalry / infantry).
- Freshly spawned player-faction soldiers wander naturally: they do not follow you and are never teleported to you until you assign them to a squad or give them an order.
- Command a single unit, a whole army or a whole faction with the Control Tool: move, attack, follow.
- Outside creative mode, crouch-right-click only opens the unit screen of soldiers or commanders in your own player faction; use it to inspect status, manage gear (empty slots = its own gear) and tune strategies for that single unit only. Creative mode can open any faction's unit screen.
- Use the command wheel ({key.wheel}) for formations, attacks, movement, riding and squad commands (the recruit-nearby radius is player-common.toml -> enlistNearbyRadius).
- Open the faction screen ({key.faction}) to view and edit hostility and alliances between factions.
- Use the RTS view ({key.rts}) to box-select and command large armies.
- Use the Hatred Wand to mark a unit / faction hostile, or to clear in-game hostility.
- Use the Retrieval Tool to pack a soldier into a spawn egg, keeping faction, form and tier.
- Use the tactical equipment slots ({key.equipment}) for tactical gear: warm clothes (freeze immunity), the horse whistle (summon / ride your war horse) and ammo boxes (ammo reserve).
- Summon your own war horse with the horse whistle; ride form toggles are {key.cavalry} / {key.infantry}.
guide.monster_conquest.chapter.world.bod:
#Village patrols
- Villager patrols spawn naturally with villages: up to 3 per village, each with 1 captain + 3 soldiers (including the four gunners).
- A new squad only spawns while the village has fewer than 3 captains AND there is room for its 3 soldiers within the 9-soldier cap (current soldiers <= 6), so a lost captain is not replaced immediately.
- Spawning only requires the vanilla village check (claimed beds / workstations nearby); villagers are NOT required, so walled-in or buried villagers no longer stop patrols. Spawn positions are safety-checked too.
- Patrols, combat and targeting never leave the village range; when a villager is attacked the patrols defend it like iron golems.
- Only naturally spawned units are affected; spawn eggs, commands and player-recruited units keep their normal behaviour.
- Toggle & tuning: config/monster_conquest/factions-common.toml -> villageSpawn.villager.

#Raid reinforcements
- Each time a raid spawns a new wave, the illager faction immediately sends a random number of patrol squads: they spawn together with that wave's raiders, and the higher the wave, the more squads (up to 5 per wave).
- Reinforcement soldiers come with much better gear: 85% roll above T0 by default (vs 15% for normal summons), weighted towards T3 / T4; tune with raidSpawn.illager.highTierChance.
- Reinforcements count as part of the raid: every reinforcement unit is counted individually in the "raiders remaining" number and boss bar (one-to-one with vanilla raiders).
- Ringing a bell during a raid highlights the reinforcements just like vanilla raiders.
- During a raid, village patrols keep every raid unit locked in their target list (no line of sight needed, no mid-raid drop) until the raid ends.
- Reinforcements patrol, fight and target only near the raid centre; survivors withdraw (despawn) once the raid ends.
- Toggle & tuning: config/monster_conquest/factions-common.toml -> raidSpawn.illager.

guide.monster_conquest.chapter.path.body:
#Crafting
- 1 stick + 1 lime dye (same family as the Retrieval Tool and Control Tool).

#Left-click: walking mode
- Patrol: units visit your points in order and loop back to the first one after the last.
- Route: units visit the points in order and stop at the last one, going back to free roaming.
- Sneak + left-click switches between Army mode and Single mode.

#Sneak + left-click: selection scope
- Army mode: middle-clicking a unit selects its whole NPC army / patrol squad (the leader walks, soldiers follow the march trail), or a player-faction small squad. Units without a group fall back to being selected alone.
- Single mode: only that one unit. If it belongs to a player small squad it first leaves the squad (squad id cleared) so a route set for it never drags the whole squad along.

- Survival players can only use it on their own units / squads: aiming at someone else’s or at an NPC unit is refused (creative can use it on anything).

#Middle-click: pick a target
- On a unit: select it with the scope above (the action bar shows what got selected and how many points it has).
- On a spawn point block: select the spawn point - the route you draw stays in sync with units already spawned there and future spawns; after an edit, existing units restart on the new route (spawn point routes are creative-only).

#Right-click: add points / sneak + right-click: clear
- Right-click: add the spot you are aiming at - like the other tools it uses the crosshair ray, up to 256 blocks, so you can point far away; the point is the block above whatever the crosshair hits (looking at the sky uses 16 blocks ahead).
- Sneak + right-click: clear every path point of the current selection.
- While held, the top-right corner shows the walking mode, selection scope, current target and path point count, just like the other tools.
- While you hold the Path Tool, the world draws the points set for the current target: every point is labelled with its index, and lines with arrows between points show the direction of travel (patrol mode also draws a last-point-to-first-point loop arrow).

#Lifetime of a route
- Routes live in the current world only (stored per unit / squad / army / spawn point) and are never written into blocks or eggs:
  - breaking, middle-click copying or turning a spawn point into an item never carries the route; a re-placed one starts with none;
  - packing a soldier (or a whole army) into eggs never stores the route, so units come back without one.
- The Clear button in the spawn point screen removes the route set for that spawn point; units already spawned there stop the old route too, and later spawns start without one.
- Units with a combat target finish the fight first and then continue; after finishing a route the unit returns to its normal behaviour (free roaming for NPC units).

guide.monster_conquest.chapter.facilitie:
#Recruitment Station
- Crafted from 8 stone + 1 diamond; its "spawn face" points at the player when placed, and recruited soldiers appear right next to that face.
- Right-click to open the screen and recruit by tier. Every tier costs amethyst shards, and recruiting or upgrading to T4 also costs 1 nether star. A soldier egg from one tier lower can be upgraded for half of the target tier's base price.
- Recruits join your player faction and hold position next to the station.

#Trade Station
- Crafted from 8 planks + 1 emerald; right-click to buy ammo, guns and tactical tools at crafting-material prices, in bulk (Shift+click = buy x64).

#Spawn Point
- Not craftable: take it from the creative inventory, or middle-click an existing spawn point. A pickaxe is the right tool, and breaking it drops a block item carrying the current settings.
- Direction: the "spawn face" points at the player when placed (all six directions work, walls and ceilings included); spawned units appear right next to that face and face away from it - put simply, it spawns out of the side it faces.
- Right-click the block to open the screen (or left-click while holding the spawn point item to edit the settings stored inside it); the screen is creative-only, but survival players can still use an already-configured spawn point. In the screen you pick the unit (commander / patrol captain / soldier), faction, infantry / cavalry form and soldier gear tier T0~T4.
- Commanders and patrol captains belong to their own faction: the faction row is locked to it, and they always spawn as that faction; only soldiers use the faction you pick.
- Template egg: put any unit spawn egg into the slot at the bottom left and the spawn point uses it instead - tier, gear, faction and form match that egg exactly, and the egg is never consumed. While an egg is in the slot it wins and the unit list is locked, and the faction / form / tier rows show the egg’s own values (player factions included). A fresh soldier egg carries no faction data yet, so inserting it stamps your own player faction into it (same as placing that egg); take it out to pick a unit manually again.
- Counts and timing: "per spawn" (default 0) and "interval" (default unlimited) - nothing spawns until you set them; "total limit" caps how many it may ever create (press Reset to start over), and "alive limit" caps how many of its units may exist at once (spawning pauses until the count drops).
- The top-right button is the spawn switch (off by default); spawning pauses while the screen is open and starts timing once you close it.
- Admins can run /monsterc spawnpoints off to disable every spawn point (on to restore, toggle to flip); while disabled, the switch in the screen shows "Off (global)" and is greyed out.
- Every spawn point keeps its settings inside the block: middle-click copy and drops both carry the settings (template egg included), so replacing it keeps everything.
- Spawned units stay in the world (they never despawn), so use the total / alive limits to keep them in check.
- Spawn points and the recruitment station now include Vex and Allay soldiers. They are fixed-tier flying units: Vex can fly through walls, while Allay keeps block collision and follows air routes around walls. The UI omits meaningless tier and riding controls for them.
- Fixed-size facility and unit screens scale down to fit the current display; the guide book narrows its chapter sidebar on small screens.
- Press {key.lobby} to open the auto battler lobby: create a room, search or join by room code, ready up, toggle AI fill for empty seats, and let the host manage seats and start.
- Starting a match shows the child-server launch, world loading and player transfer stages with an ETA. The isolated flat-void world stays at noon with its arena base at Y=0. Every preparation phase returns living players to separate home boards whose numbers stay bound to their room seats, and each battle randomly uses one participant's home as the venue. Leaving the game during a match counts as a surrender and retains the placement record.
- Stages have seven rounds and are labelled 1-1, 1-7, 2-1 and so on. The BossBar shows your level/XP and gold, the opponent's level and gold, the phase, stage-round and countdown.
- Entering the next preparation phase grants 2 XP. Fixed income is 2 at 1-2/1-3, 3 from 1-4 through 1-7, 4 at 2-1, and 5 from 2-2 onward. Interest grants 1 per 10 held (maximum 5); a win grants 1, and win/loss streak bonuses grant 1 at 2-4, 2 at 5 and 3 at 6 or more.
- Integrated singleplayer supports AI matches and LAN testing; the main world temporarily unloads during the arena match and reopens automatically when it finishes.
- During a match, {key.lobby} opens the unit controls. The shop sells one-star cards whose 1-5 cost prices and odds are owned by the auto battler pool; levels run to 10, and three matching units merge up to three stars. The equipment bag combines components; select an item and click a unit to equip it, including deployed units during battle. Selling a unit returns its items, and a remover returns all items from a unit. AI opponents use exactly the same gold, XP, shop refresh, purchase and merge rules as players.
- Preparation changes on the 9x5 home half-board and nine-slot bench are mirrored to physical arena units in real time. During battle the board is locked, but shopping, refreshing and XP purchases remain available; only bench movement and bench sales are accepted. While the GUI is open, use D to refresh, F to buy XP, E to sell the selected unit, and Space to return to your home board. The portrait column is sorted by health and labels each player's home-board number; winners are green, losers red and unresolved combatants grey during battle, with colors resetting after combat. Combat units show overhead health values, green for your units and red for enemies, and arena units omit main-world faction overlays. Surrender requires confirmation; eliminated players remain read-only spectators and may exit the world.
guide.monster_conquest.chapter.logic.ext:
- Flying units use 3D air pathfinding. An installed route keeps navigation ownership; when a path node clips a wall corner, a full-collision-box air detour is inserted before reconnecting. Greedy straight-line movement must not cancel a maze route each tick.
- Flying wander and combat use bounded hover altitude so units neither settle into the floor nor climb forever while chasing each other.
guide.monster_conquest.chapter.facilitie: - Spawn points and the recruitment station use the same unit capability rules. Vex and Allay are fixed-tier flying soldiers and do not consume the formal army cap; summons remain defined by summon ownership, independent of whether they fly.
